claim: the final K1 architecture achieved strong generalization on the untouched Final Holdout
caveat: Macro F1 0.920177; Top-2 0.990610; Holdout first accessed once.

claim: incident-level stacking materially improved classification/ranking compared with mean probability aggregation
caveat: TRAIN-only Macro F1 gain 0.131729 over K1-B0 mean aggregation.

claim: RPKI/ROV features contributed strongly to Hijack classification
caveat: Supported by TRAIN ablation; phrase as predictive contribution, not causal proof.

claim: CAIDA/peer-visibility context contributed useful signal for Leak/Outage
caveat: Supported by feature-family experiments; avoid causal overclaiming.

claim: XGBoost outperformed refined Random Forest under the selected architecture
caveat: Phase I2 XGB Macro F1 0.805678 vs H2 RF 0.784588.

claim: the final system ranked the true class in the Top-2 for 211 of 213 Holdout incidents
Outage was the strongest final class
Hijack remained the most difficult final class
caveat: Hijack F1 0.877698, lowest of the three classes.

claim: leakage controls and permutation testing supported the validity of K1
caveat: Supports absence of detected leakage, not a mathematical proof.

claim: model features identify root cause mechanisms causally
caveat: Current evidence is predictive classification/ranking, not causal inference.
